blocks.text: SUGGESTED ACTIVITIES FOR STUDENTS REGARDING THIS UNIT (a) The student may use pH paper in determining the pH of fresh juices of various vegetables and fruits, soft drinks, body fluids and also that of water samples available. (b) The pH paper may also be used to determine the pH of different salt solutions and from that he/she may determine if these are formed from strong/weak acids and bases. (c) They may prepare some buffer solutions by mixing the solutions of sodium acetate and acetic acid and determine their pH using pH paper. (d) They may be provided with different indicators to observe their colours in solutions of varying pH. (e) They may perform some acid-base titrations using indicators. (f) They may observe common ion effect on the solubility of sparingly soluble salts. (g) If pH meter is available in their school, they may measure the pH with it and compare the results obtained with that of the pH paper.

6.1 A liquid is in equilibrium with its vapour in a sealed container at a fixed temperature. The volume of the container is suddenly increased. a) What is the initial effect of the change on vapour pressure? b) How do rates of evaporation and condensation change initially? c) What happens when equilibrium is restored finally and what will be the final vapour pressure?
6.2 What is Kc for the following equilibrium when the equilibrium concentration of each substance is: [SO2]= 0.60M, [O2] = 0.82M and [SO3] = 1.90M ?
6.3 At a certain temperature and total pressure of 105Pa, iodine vapour contains 40% by volume of I atoms

note: Single-column end-of-chapter page: the green 'SUGGESTED ACTIVITIES' panel, then the EXERCISES banner and exercises 6.1 to 6.5. previous_page_last_block was null in the input, so I judged the opening continuation against the page 40 output file I wrote myself: page 40 closed the SUMMARY panel on a complete sentence and had blank space below it, so first_block_continues_from_previous is false. The activities panel is kept as one box block, its own bold banner line included, because the banner sits inside the panel's rule and is not a running header. Left for the special transcriber: the three centred reaction equations that interrupt the exercises (block 5, the 2SO2/O2/2SO3 equilibrium of 6.2; block 7, the I2/2I equilibrium of 6.3) and the two indented reaction lists (block 10, the five reactions (i)-(v) of 6.4; block 12, the two equilibria of 6.5 with their Kp values) - the text layer breaks every double equilibrium arrow onto its own blank line and scrambles the subscripts, so these are marked rather than transcribed. In block 6 the pressure is written '105Pa' exactly as the text layer has it; on the page it is printed as ten to the power five Pa. last_block_continues_on_next is false: exercise 6.5 finishes on the page and the bottom fifth of the page is blank, so nothing is cut off, even though the exercise list itself runs on to page 42.
